$comment: Installs that do not come from a hashed lock and are allowed to stay so (SEC-SC-07, C6.44; scripts/supply_chain.py check, rules PY-INSTALL and NODE-NPX). Each entry excuses the commands of `file` that contain `match` for `rule`, with the reason, and the follow-up that removes it where there is one. An entry that excuses nothing fails the check, so the list only shrinks as installs move to a lock.

installs.reason: The hashed installer itself. Its callers pass --require-hashes for every lock; the vcs lock pins commits and the project goes in with --no-deps.

The generated or released Python SDK under test, from its own pyproject with its dependencies resolved as its users' installs resolve them: that install is what the suite tests. Its test tools come before it from the hashed integration-tests/sdk_tests/requirements/tests.lock.
A person's acceptance check of the demo connector against a running stack, with the published SDK as a user installs it; no CI job or image runs it.

The cost-class benchmark's own client and corpus generators (reportlab, python-docx, openpyxl, Pillow, numpy, pypdfium2), in a throwaway venv on a manually or weekly dispatched runner; nothing it installs reaches an image or a release. Follow-up: lock them in integration-tests/uv.lock and install with uv sync --locked.
